entries.name: Routine collapse
entries.definition: Participant describes pre-fire routines breaking down or becoming impossible to maintain — sleep, work, parenting, exercise, social rhythms.
examples: all my routines were… were done

entries.name: Displacement instability
entries.definition: Multiple moves, hotel-hopping, uncertainty about temporary housing, or the practical labor of finding a place to live.

entries.name: Recovery as second job
entries.definition: Participant describes recovery tasks (insurance, paperwork, contractors) consuming hours equivalent to a job on top of normal life or paid work.

entries.name: Competing caregiving demands
entries.definition: Participant managing recovery while also caring for children, aging parents, ill partners, or pets — multi-front burden.

entries.name: Career or education disruption
entries.definition: Job loss, role change, leaving school, going part-time, or feeling unable to function professionally because of recovery demands.

entries.name: Children's schooling disruption
entries.definition: Loss of school, difficulty placing children, navigating educational continuity for kids during displacement.

entries.name: Grief over irreplaceable items
entries.definition: Specific, named losses that carry symbolic or emotional weight — heirlooms, photographs, art, family archives — beyond their replacement value.

entries.name: Loss of home as anchor
entries.definition: The home itself, or 'going home', as an emotional/identity anchor whose absence is destabilizing.

entries.name: Intrusive imagery / acute trauma response
entries.definition: Vivid involuntary recall, nightmares, hypervigilance, dissociation, or other acute trauma responses.

entries.name: Moral injury / systemic injustice
entries.definition: Distress framed as injustice rather than misfortune — institutional failures, inequity, neglect of vulnerable neighbors.

entries.name: Delayed emotional processing
entries.definition: Participant describes pushing emotion aside to function during acute phase, or grief surfacing only later when logistics ease.

entries.name: Hope from visible progress
entries.definition: Tangible recovery milestones (debris cleared, foundation, plants regrowing, neighbors returning) restoring hope.

entries.name: Isolation / friction with un-affected world
entries.definition: Difficulty being around people whose lives weren't disrupted, or feeling forgotten as public attention moves on.

entries.name: Meaning through helping others
entries.definition: Volunteering, advocacy, mentoring other survivors as a way to convert pain into purpose.

entries.name: Comparative luck appraisal
entries.definition: Participant repeatedly frames their own recovery as exceptionally fortunate by reference to worse-off others. Functions as both a coping mechanism and acknowledgment of inequity in disaster outcomes. Distinct from gratitude or relief — the comparison itself is the load-bearing element.
examples: I'm lucky compared to most people
we got off easy compared to what our neighbors are dealing with

entries.name: Witnessing burden / secondary load
entries.definition: Emotional weight from witnessing the suffering of other survivors, distinct from one's own grief and from friction with the un-affected world. Often co-occurs with comparative_luck_appraisal but the two can be separated by who the participant is centering: oneself (luck appraisal) vs. others (witnessing burden).
examples: it's heavy because they're going through a lot worse than me

entries.name: Insurance as adversarial system
entries.definition: Insurer behavior that requires constant self-advocacy: delays, denials, lowballing, repeated retelling of trauma, demands for documentation.

entries.name: Permitting and rebuild bureaucracy
entries.definition: County permitting, code compliance, contractor coordination, septic/utility complexity that participants feel unprepared for.

entries.name: Fragmented information landscape
entries.definition: Resources exist but are scattered across agencies, channels, and groups; participant must aggregate and verify themselves.

entries.name: Executive functioning impairment
entries.definition: Cognitive overload that collapses sequencing, prioritization, and decision bandwidth — not motivation, but capacity.

entries.name: Contamination / standing-home limbo
entries.definition: Specific to homes that survived structurally but are chemically contaminated. Pathways unclear, insurance pushes return, no standards.

entries.name: Inventory burden
entries.definition: The labor and emotional weight of itemizing lost belongings, often hundreds or thousands of items, often without receipts.

entries.name: Financial strain and tax complexity
entries.definition: Pressure from underinsurance, SBA loans, mortgage relief paperwork, tax implications of settlements.

entries.name: Lack of a case manager / navigator
entries.definition: Explicit desire for a single human (or system) to offload the cognitive and logistical burden of sequencing recovery tasks.

entries.name: Immediate logistics (acute phase)
entries.definition: Housing, basic supplies, paperwork, utilities — first weeks.

entries.name: Resource navigation (medium phase)
entries.definition: FEMA, insurance, aid programs, legal — the medium-term grind.

entries.name: Emotional normalization (later phase)
entries.definition: Anticipatory psychoeducation about what to expect at 3/6/12 months, grief processing, integration.

entries.name: Long-term planning
entries.definition: Tax strategy, financial planning, identity reconstruction, decisions about staying or leaving.

entries.name: Social media as information hub
entries.definition: Facebook groups, Discord, WeChat, WhatsApp, Slack used to crowdsource real-time, situationally relevant recovery information.

entries.name: Self-built spreadsheets / docs
entries.definition: Participant created or adopted DIY tools (Google Drive, spreadsheets, notebooks) to track inventory, contacts, deadlines.

entries.name: AI-assisted inventory
entries.definition: Using LLMs or photo-recognition tools to reconstruct lost household contents, often by extrapolating from purchase history or photos.

entries.name: AI as advocacy tool
entries.definition: Using AI to draft dispute letters, decode adjuster reports, identify code violations, or strengthen leverage in adversarial systems.

entries.name: No fit-for-purpose app
entries.definition: Participant tried productivity or recovery apps and found none adequate for the complexity and cross-domain nature of recovery.

entries.name: AI useful for practical/cognitive load
entries.definition: Endorses AI for synthesis, paperwork, sourcing information, reducing executive load.

entries.name: Skeptical of AI for emotional support
entries.definition: Prefers human connection for emotional processing; concerned about over-reliance, dependency, or unsafe attachment.

entries.name: Hallucination / accuracy concern
entries.definition: Verification burden, fabricated regulatory or insurance claims, distrust without human oversight.

entries.name: Wants human accountability layer
entries.definition: Endorses AI only when tethered to a real human, professional oversight, or visible safety guardrails.

entries.name: Judgment-free disclosure
entries.definition: Finds AI easier to talk to honestly than humans because of reduced fear of judgment.

entries.name: Tone too affirming / sycophantic
entries.definition: Off-the-shelf LLM tone is too 'nice' and lacks the grounded honesty survivors need.

entries.name: Endorses centralized resource hub
entries.definition: Positive response to one-stop / centralized recovery information.

entries.name: Endorses contextual / personalized AI
entries.definition: Positive response to AI having context on the user's specific recovery journey.

entries.name: Endorses community / public-channel layer
entries.definition: Positive response to summarizing public group chats, surfacing relevant items.

entries.name: Endorses tracker / captain's-log function
entries.definition: Positive response to AI maintaining a recovery log, deadlines, reminders.

entries.name: Concern about accuracy / hallucination
entries.definition: Hesitation about model reliability, especially for legal/insurance use.

entries.name: Concern about AI mental-health use
entries.definition: Hesitation about AI for emotional support, dependency, or unsafe attachment.

entries.name: Privacy / data concern
entries.definition: Hesitation about data handling, confidentiality, where information goes.

entries.name: Tone / over-affirming concern
entries.definition: Hesitation that AI feedback is too soothing, generic, or non-critical.

entries.name: Specific feature request
entries.definition: Concrete suggestion: e.g. cross-disaster scope, tracker fields, multimodal access, integration with X.

entries.name: Relevance beats volume
entries.definition: Recurring observation that the issue isn't lack of information but lack of *situationally precise* information for one's exact recovery profile.

entries.name: Timing of support matters
entries.definition: Different needs at different phases; emotional support may not land in the acute phase, where logistics dominate.

entries.name: Human contact remains irreplaceable
entries.definition: Across many forms of help, participant explicitly distinguishes what AI can do from what only a human can.
